Why did Pulsar bring back the same two nurses?
25 years. One ad. One twist.

2001
Two nurses. A maternity ward. A motorcycle.
“It’s a boy!”

2026
Same nurses. Something familiar under a white sheet. Déjà vu.
“It’s a bad boy.”

It skips the setup.
You already know the joke, so the film spends its time on the twist. Ogilvy’s Sukesh Nayak says the familiarity builds anticipation, then the film surprises you.

One word moves the brand.
Boy → bad boy.
Same scene, new meaning. Bajaj Auto’s marketing head says the essence stays “Definitely Daring”.

A scene people remember is a memory shortcut.
Marketers call these distinctive brand assets. Keep the asset recognisable. Change what it means.

It’s talking to two audiences.
If you saw the 2001 ad, you get the wink. If you didn’t, you still get a strange, memorable little story.

Find the one thing customers already remember.
A line. A scene. A colour. A character. Reuse it. Change only the meaning.

Which old ad should come back next?
Tell me in the comments. Follow for more brand decodes.
Sources: afaqs (15 Sep 2026), Campaign Brief Asia (16 Sep 2026), Medianews4u.
